summary: Shows how to make managed nodes use Python 3 by setting ansible_python_interpreter per host or group in inventory, in ansible.cfg, or with -e for testing; Ansible also auto-detects Python 3 on many platforms.
questions: How do I tell Ansible to use /usr/bin/python3 on remote hosts?
Can I set the Python interpreter for a whole group of hosts?
How can I quickly test a playbook under Python 3?
Does Ansible detect Python 3 automatically on managed nodes?

answer_card.title: Use Python 3 on managed nodes
answer_card.answer_md:
Ansible auto-detects Python 3 on many platforms. To set it explicitly, use `ansible_python_interpreter`:

```ini
localhost-py3 ansible_host=localhost ansible_connection=local ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3

[py3_hosts]
ubuntu16
fedora27

[py3_hosts:vars]
ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3
```

You can also set a default in `ansible.cfg`, or test ad hoc:

```shell
ansible-playbook sample-playbook.yml -e 'ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3'
```
